tasks.title: Public Libraries: Access and Responsibility
tasks.instruction: Write an essay discussing two of the points in your notes. You should explain which point you think is more important for the future of public libraries, giving reasons in support of your answer. You may, if you wish, make use of the opinions expressed in the discussion, but you should use your own words as far as possible.

promptBlocks.text: Your class has listened to a radio discussion about how public libraries should balance free access with long-term financial responsibility. You have made the notes below.

promptBlocks.heading: Priorities for public libraries
listItems: maintaining free access for all residents
investing in digital resources and online services
partnering with local businesses to generate income

promptBlocks.heading: Opinions expressed in the discussion
paragraphs: Free access is the whole point of a public library. If we start charging, we lose the trust of the community.
Digital resources are the future. Libraries that don't invest in e-books and online databases will become irrelevant.
Business partnerships can bring in money, but they might push libraries to prioritise profit over public need.

tasks.title: Proposal for a Library Outreach Programme
tasks.instruction:
Write a proposal for the regional library network director. In your proposal, you should:

• assess the effectiveness of current outreach efforts
• recommend two new initiatives to reach underserved communities
• explain how these initiatives would benefit both the library and the community

promptBlocks.text: The regional library network is reviewing its outreach programme, which aims to bring library services to communities that currently have limited access. The network director has invited proposals for improving the programme's effectiveness. You decide to write a proposal.

tasks.title: Email to Programme Coordinator
tasks.instruction:
Write an email to the programme coordinator. In your email, you should:

• explain why you think the proposed changes are necessary
• analyse one potential negative consequence of the changes
• propose a way to address that consequence while still moving forward

promptBlocks.text: You are a library user representative on a regional library network planning committee. The committee is considering a proposal to reduce opening hours at several branches to save money. The programme coordinator has asked for your views on the proposal.

tasks.title: Review of a Library Event Series
tasks.instruction:
Write a review for the regional library network's website. In your review, you should:

• describe the event series and its aims
• evaluate how well it achieved those aims
• recommend whether the series should be continued or modified

promptBlocks.text: You see this announcement on a regional library network website.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted: Library event series
paragraphs: Have you attended any of our 'Libraries Connect' events this year? These events aimed to bring together library users and local organisations to discuss community needs. We would like to hear your views on how successful the series has been and whether it should continue.
Send us your review and we will publish the best ones on our website.
